Lessons

  • Digital Humanities Crash Course

    • What are the Digital Humanities?

      This introduction outlines the arguments and ideas which guide conversations in the digital humanities. It also defines, more broadly, what the 'Digital Health Humanities' are.

    • Low Code Approaches to Digital Humanities Research Methods

      This hands-on lesson will teach learners about the basic principles that guide humanistic research. Using a low code approach, where learners need no technical skill to learn, this lesson will teach the basic ideas that form the use of digital methodologies in humanistic research.

    • Applying Digital Methods to Your Research

      Building on the previous two lessons in the Digital Humanities Crash Course, this lesson will teach learners about a variety of different digital methods, encouraging to think about the best methods that can be used to answer their research questions.

    • The International Image Interoperability Framework (IIIF)

      This introduction outlines the arguments and ideas which guide conversations in the digital humanities. It also defines, more broadly, what the 'Digital Health Humanities' are.

  • Managing Projects in the Digital Health Humanities

    • Digital Workflows

  • Data Ethics

    • Introduction to Data Ethics

      This lesson introduces learners to ethical concepts developed in public humanities research, and applies them to issues in the digital health humanities.

The Digital Health Humanities Toolkit was developed at the University of Californa San Francisco thanks to a grant from the National Endowment for the Humanities.
